authoritative.pre: BIND publishes these records. Point the domain to
authoritative.unconfigured: No shared nameservers are set on the server, so these are only a placeholder and cannot be given to a customer.

valueHint.CNAME: Target domain name, for example target.example.com
valueHint.MX: Mail server, for example mail.example.com (priority is set separately)
valueHint.TXT: Free-form text, for example v=spf1 mx ~all
valueHint.SRV: weight port target, for example 5 5060 sip.example.com (priority is set separately)
valueHint.PTR: Target domain name, for example host.example.com
valueHint.DS: keytag algorithm digest-type digest, for example 12345 13 2 49FD46E6C4B45C55D4AC...
valueHint.TLSA: usage selector matching-type data, for example 3 1 1 0B9FA5A59EED715C26C1020C...

dnssec.title: DNSSEC
dnssec.description: Signs this zone with BIND inline signing. Add the generated DS record at your domain registrar.
dnssec.dsHint: Add this DS record in your registrar's DNSSEC settings. Propagation may take up to the record TTL.
dnssec.signingInProgress: Signing is still in progress. Refresh the status after a few seconds.
dnssec.enabledMsg: DNSSEC enabled. Add the DS record below at your domain registrar.

actions.exportTitle: Download the DNS records as a BIND zone file

import.title: Import Zone File
import.description: Upload a standard BIND zone file (.zone / .txt). Records are imported into this domain, then the zone is validated and rewritten.
import.overwriteLabel: Overwrite existing records — when unchecked, records are merged (new ones added)
import.replaceWarning: ⚠️ ALL current DNS records for this domain will be deleted and replaced with the file's. Exporting a backup first is recommended.

bulkDelete.title: Delete selected DNS records
bulkDelete.message: {{count}} DNS records will be permanently deleted. This action cannot be undone. Continue?

dnssecDisable.title: Disable DNSSEC
dnssecDisable.message: Remove the DS record at your domain registrar and wait for its TTL before disabling DNSSEC. Otherwise the domain may stop resolving with SERVFAIL. Continue only after the DS record has been removed.

modal.nameHint: “@” is the root domain. Other examples include “www” and “mail”.

ipv6.title: IPv6 address
ipv6.hint: The address this domain answers on over IPv6. Changing it rewrites the domain's AAAA records.
ipv6.saveFailed: The address could not be saved.
ipv6.clearWarning: Clearing the address removes this domain's AAAA records, so IPv6 clients will fall back to IPv4.
ipv6.noRoutable: This server carries no globally routable IPv6 address, so no AAAA record can be published.
ipv6.noStack: This server has no IPv6 at all. The panel serves every site over IPv4 only.

reasons.ipv6_not_local: This server does not answer on that address. Publishing it would make the site unreachable for IPv6 clients and stop certificate renewal.
reasons.ipv6_not_v6: That is an IPv4 address. This field takes an IPv6 address.
reasons.ipv6_invalid: That is not a valid IP address.

verify.title: DNS verification
verify.hint: asks a public resolver what is actually published
verify.failed: The DNS check could not be run.

reasons.unreadable: The lookup failed, so the record could not be read.
reasons.elsewhere: The record does not point at this server.
reasons.aaaa_missing: No AAAA record is published, so IPv6 clients cannot reach this domain.
reasons.aaaa_elsewhere: The AAAA record points somewhere else. IPv6 clients go there instead, and certificate renewal fails because Let's Encrypt tries IPv6 first.
reasons.aaaa_unmanaged: An AAAA record is published but no IPv6 address is assigned here, so the panel cannot tell whether it is correct.

ns.missing: The domain has no nameserver records; check that it is registered and active.
ns.partial: Only one of the nameservers belongs to this server; set both at the registrar.
ns.elsewhere: The domain is not delegated to this panel, so its DNS is served elsewhere and the records below were read from there. Changes made in this panel will NOT go live; update them at that provider.

a.missing: The domain does not resolve to any address.

mail_a.missing: {{host}} does not resolve, so mail cannot be delivered: the MX record points at it.
mail_a.elsewhere: {{host}} does not point at this server.

mx.missing: There is no MX record, so this domain cannot receive mail.
mx.elsewhere: Mail is routed to another server, which is expected if you use an external mail service.

spf.missing: There is no SPF record, so the mail you send may be treated as spam.
spf.multiple: There is more than one SPF record, which makes SPF invalid altogether. Keep exactly one.
spf.unauthorized: The SPF record does not appear to authorize this server; it has no matching ip4, a or mx mechanism.

dkim.no_key: No DKIM key has been generated for this domain in the panel.
dkim.missing: The {{host}} TXT record is not published.
dkim.mismatch: The published DKIM key differs from the one the panel generated, so signatures cannot be verified.

dmarc.missing: There is no DMARC record. It is not required, but it improves deliverability.
dmarc.malformed: A TXT record exists but it does not start with v=DMARC1.

ptr.ptr_missing: The sending address has no PTR record. Most large providers refuse mail from an address without one; ask whoever provides the server to set it.
ptr.ptr_no_forward_match: The PTR names a host that does not resolve back to this address. A receiving server treats that the same as having no PTR at all.
ptr.no_server_address: The server has no public IPv4 address on record, so reverse DNS could not be checked.

mail_ports.ports_closed: Some mail ports could not be reached from the server itself, which means the service is stopped or a local firewall rule closed them.
mail_ports.all_ports_closed: No mail port could be reached from the server itself. Mail is not being served at all.
mail_ports.no_server_address: The server has no public IPv4 address on record, so the ports could not be checked.
